investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) This offence applies from the 28th June 2022 due to changes made by section 86 of the Police, Crime, Sentencing and Courts Act 2022, which increased the penalty on indictment from 14 years imprisonment to life imprisonment. For the offence applying before the 28th June 2022, see H8762.
(ii) The minimum period of obligatory disqualification for this offence under section 34 of the Road Traffic Offenders Act 1988 was increased by section 86 of the Police, Crime, Sentencing and Courts Act 2022. See section 34(3), 34(3A) and 34(4ZA) which in some cases, increases the disqualification period to ten or five years.
(iii) See section 24 of the Road Traffic Offenders Act 1988 for alternative verdicts.
(iv) For the more usual offence wordings relating to the failure to provide specimens see H29 (drive/attempt to drive) and H30 (in charge).
(v) This offence was inserted by section 31 of the Road Safety Act 2006.
(vi) Officers should ensure that they know the C.P.S. guidelines for this offence before preparing any charges. When investigating these offences consideration must be given to the advice offered in the charging standards.
